simplified: Your dreams can give you ideas about things you didn't know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing your teeth, or being naked in public, usually mean similar things for many people. But to really understand what they mean for you, you need to link them to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

One interesting case of wild animals living in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. There are about 35,000 wild dogs on the streets of Moscow. Some dogs were born wild, and some were pets that people left behind. Some dogs live alone, and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied these dogs and found that they have adapted very well to city life. They have learned it is safer to cross the street with people, and some dogs seem to understand traffic lights.

Wonder is RJ Palacio's first book. On her website, she says she got the idea for the story after seeing a girl with a facial difference on the street. Wonder has sold many copies in the United States and has won several awards. Many schools are using it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is being made, and many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe has two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows they are not usual pets and has often tried to explain that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if cared for properly. She understands why some people don’t like them. Chloe didn’t like rats at first until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how friendly and smart they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to have two of them.

Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have been shocked by electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce problems with people, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to chase baboons away from the city or catch them and release them in the countryside. This plan has worked a bit, but it is hard to stop baboons from returning to the city when they find easy food.

I work for a big IT company, but since their main office is in the U.S., I do my job online from home. This way, I don’t waste time traveling or chatting with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this flexibility is important to me because I can take time off when my kids have school events or if I need to see the dentist. The downside is that without set working hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

In the 1990s, graffiti was still common, but street art became very popular worldwide. Some artists wanted to make political statements and created art to make people think about war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists focused on making beautiful art. In South America, many street artists worked in poor areas to add color and beauty to dull city walls.

Social media, magazines, and store displays show people many things to buy, and British shoppers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking, and big brands sell cheap clothes that people can throw away after wearing them a few times.

Sam squinted at the sun and saw the dust from the car going to the Big House. The horses were swatting flies and didn’t care that their owner was visiting after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter only came out when he needed to, which was good for Sam. The more he stayed away from his boss, the longer he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. The wet spots on his shirt looked like shapes on a map. His skin was getting red in the June sun. He looked like a man who made money while others worked.

Many people in Berlin, Germany, said that shooting pigs was too cruel, and there were strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council decided to take a kinder approach to deal with the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they built fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. We will see if this plan works, but it might be hard because warmer winters mean there are more pigs now.

An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of Greek myths. When she was a child, one of her favorite stories was about Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, Athens is controlled by Crete, but the people of Athens fight back. As a punishment, the king of Crete, Minos, makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The young people are put into a maze and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. But one of the boys, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne thinks of Katniss Everdeen as a modern Theseus.

Zoos can teach people about protecting animals and their homes by bringing people and animals together. Some zoos help animals that were hurt in circuses or were left behind as pets. They also do important research on how animals behave and how to help them when they are sick.

A new trend is starting against buying too much – the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US, where it is a way to say no to spending too much on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, people protest and cut their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups help people exchange and fix things they already have.

Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on how you see it, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is seen as vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police, and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils say it costs a lot to clean graffiti off buildings, buses, and trains.

What do people in the art world think about graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as valuable art. There have been big exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists by saying, "Artists who paint on the street are just expressing themselves and not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated."

Most people have four to six dreams every night after they turn ten, which means they can have about 2,000 dreams each year. By the time they are 80 years old, a person might have had around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95 to 99 percent of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand dreams in our lives. It’s easy to think that sometimes a dream can happen before something similar occurs in real life, especially if the dream is about something we see often.

The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem and has twelve poor areas controlled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol has all the power. Each area makes different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth area, but they fought against the Capitol before and were destroyed.

Wild animals often come into cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started going into homes near the city to eat. They open trash bins and take fruit from gardens. Some bold baboons have even entered houses and taken food from kitchens! Baboons can be dangerous and have attacked many pets, so many people in the city do not like them.

Many bridge accidents happen while the bridge is being built. These accidents often happen because the engineers make mistakes, like calculating wrong. The bridge can fall down because it is too heavy, which can be very dangerous for the workers on it.

George Lucas was one of the first movie directors to base his story on the 17 steps of the hero's journey. Usually, the hero starts with a normal life, but then something happens that leads them to an adventure that changes everything. At the start of Star Wars, Luke has a normal life with his aunt and uncle, fixing robots. When he discovers Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi in the robot R2D2, it is the moment that calls him to adventure and begins his journey.

Another idea to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to blow it up with a nuclear weapon. It sounds like a movie plot, like the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real plan from NASA. They would shoot eight-ton rockets at an asteroid to try to change its path. If the asteroid was too close for this to work, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to blow it up.

Campbell says that the hero first says no to the adventure, but then a mentor helps them, and they choose to go into the special world where the adventure takes place. Next, the hero faces tests, fights enemies, and meets friends to get ready for their biggest challenge. For Luke, the mentor is Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and the enemy is Darth Vader in the special world of the Death Star.

Some items that are not used much might seem useless to some people, but they can be valuable to others. With the internet, online groups have found ways to make money by sharing these items. Now, using websites and social media, it is easier for people to buy and sell second-hand things. This is called the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that dreams show things we don't know about ourselves. Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can learn about our hidden feelings and problems. The other idea was different. It said that dreams are just random thoughts in our brain while it organizes memories from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random images and feelings and make a story from them.

I work as a freelancer, which is great because I can choose what I do and how I use my time. At first, I worked from home, but it was hard to focus because there were too many distractions, like housework and family. So, I tried working at a café, but the Wi-Fi was not good, and I drank too much coffee. Finally, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with other freelancers. I liked getting ready for work in the morning and being able to concentrate in an office.

NASA can find the middle-sized asteroids if it gets the money to build a special telescope called NEOCam. If they get the money, they could reach their goal in ten years. After that, the team would need to figure out how to protect the planet from the dangerous asteroids.

The 'buy nothing' trend is now popular with social media influencers who usually post about clothes and make-up to buy. Some YouTube stars tell their viewers not to buy anything for a whole year. Two friends in Canada spent a year only buying food. For the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or home items. In the next stage, they stopped using services like haircuts, eating at restaurants, or buying gas for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

Pi thinks religion is important. His family is Hindu, but he is interested in other religions. He becomes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. When his family and teachers ask him to pick one religion, Pi says, "I just want to love God." After that, his family and teachers let him decide about religion on his own.

Some people believe that writing down your dreams can help you have clearer dreams. In lucid dreams, you know you are dreaming and can change what happens in the dream. This means you could turn a scary dream into a nice one or control the story of your dream like a movie director. So, instead of just figuring out what your dreams mean, you can create them, but you might still want to have some dreams that let your mind share its thoughts!

Some people may not know they are part of the problem with disposable clothes because they give their old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all those clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of style quickly and is often too low quality to recycle; people do not want to buy it used. A lot of it gets thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries, creating more economic and environmental issues.

Some adventurers want more than one great trip. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountains, biked across Canada, and run a long race in the Sahara Desert in very hot weather. But her most amazing trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help to get out. Many people would have stopped there, but Meagan chose to keep going. She reached the South Pole forty days later, pulling a sled with a tent and all her food through very cold weather and ice storms.

Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls of Paris. Now, he wants people to think about social issues. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to make residents think about homelessness.

In some places, local governments have tried to help artists by letting them paint in special areas instead of on random walls. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can paint freely. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city has even let some graffiti artists paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is from Cape Town, South Africa. She paints large, colorful pictures of people and animals and enjoys exploring different places. Her art can be seen on sidewalks, in empty buildings, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not last long and will be washed away by rain or cleaned up by city workers. For her, this shows how life is always changing with its endings and new beginnings.

In her last job, Gabriela was in a culture where people respected power and authority, and everyone had their place. In this culture, leaders made the big decisions and were not often questioned. However, her Swedish team was used to a culture where workers often collaborated with their bosses to solve problems and make decisions. Here, leaders act as coaches who encourage independent thinking and expect to be challenged.

When Gabriela noticed the cultural differences between her and her team, she decided to talk to them about how they felt about her leadership. Her team was happy to share their thoughts and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom to be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their jobs well. They understood that Gabriela took it personally when they tried to suggest changes to her decisions, and they explained that this was how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos são irmãos gêmeos idênticos de São Paulo. Eles pintam desde pequenas marcas até grandes e coloridas imagens de pessoas nas paredes dos prédios. Às vezes, eles precisam de guindastes para ajudar a fazer suas pinturas. Em 2007, eles pintaram todo um castelo na Escócia.

People have painted and written on walls for a long time. In ancient times, people in Africa and Europe painted pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include messages about religion, politics, love, and even some magic spells!

Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If yes, you are not alone. Every year, many people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike explorers in the past who used maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern technology like GPS and satellite phones. Many adventurers love nature and use their trips to raise awareness about environmental issues, while others want to help people in need and raise money for charities.

The first project is DART, which stands for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. They plan to test DART on a moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, called 'Didymoon,' is 150 meters wide and goes around its bigger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that DART will hit it and change its path so that telescopes on Earth can see it.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. She lost her father in a mining accident and needs to find food for her family. She hunts in the woods near District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very good at using a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is picked as one of the tributes, Katniss decides to go in her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss soon has a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details. Think about the people and places in your dreams because they might be important. After a week, you will be surprised by how much you have written. You can then connect your dreams to what happens and how you feel in your daily life.

In the past, many bridges were made of wood and could easily catch fire. This was especially true for old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could start a fire and destroy the bridge.

We cannot know how street art will change in the future, but we see some trends. Most street artists are young people who paint in their cities, but more are traveling and working in different places. Some artists use the internet to connect and share their work. The art world is also starting to recognize street art as real art. Even though we don’t know what will happen next, street art is definitely going to stay!

Suzanne has always found news about wars upsetting. When she was a child, her dad was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mom tried to protect her by not telling her about the war, but she still saw news about it and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

In a worldwide survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), over 40,000 young people and older people answered questions about work culture, communication, pay, career growth, and work-life balance. In another survey by Deloitte, more than 10,000 young people shared their views on the challenges and chances in the work world.

Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is an adventurer. He has ridden a bike in the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Erik has been blind since he was 13 years old. He also helps people with disabilities to be active and takes groups of young blind people climbing.

Online platforms are giving people a chance to make some extra money. For example, busy parents used to not sell their children's old things at local markets, but now they can sell baby clothes and equipment online to earn some cash.

Pi and Richard Parker are in the lifeboat for 227 days. They face hunger, sickness, and tiredness. They go through strong storms and the hot sun of the Pacific, but they survive. Sometimes, Pi feels comfort from his three religions, but other times he feels very lonely and sad. At last, he sees the Mexican coast, and everything changes. It would be a shame to tell you the ending, so you need to read the book to find out what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.

Chloe came home from school, made a cup of coffee, and took it to her room. She had homework, but she wanted to relax first. She liked the quiet time before her parents got home and the house became noisy with talking, TV, or her dad playing jazz while cooking. She also enjoyed this time because she could play with her pet rats.

In 2010, NASA's planetary defence team found and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' are as big as mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's path. NASA estimates there are about 50 left to record, and none of the 887 they know about are a serious threat to Earth.

Auggie decides to go to school, but he feels very nervous on his first day. Because of how he looks, it is a very hard experience for him. No one wants to sit next to him, and he sees other kids staring or whispering about him. Luckily, he makes friends with Jack and Summer. However, the first day is not the only difficult time. Auggie finds out that his classmates are afraid to touch him because they think he has 'the plague'. Throughout the school year, Auggie has many ups and downs until a surprising and upsetting event at a school camp changes everything.

The two men looked at the northern side of the land. It went on for a long way, and they could hardly see the fences. A bored teenage boy couldn't escape on foot. Sam watched the biggest horse, which was kicking the ground. He wondered if the boy could ride. There could be a lot of trouble for a good rider out there, far from anyone. But there might be even more trouble for someone who didn't know about horses and wanted to leave his father.

More than 4,000 climbers, between thirteen and eighty years old, have reached the top of Everest. Climbing high mountains in cold weather and strong storms is still very dangerous, but the best climbers in the world are now looking for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started to love mountain climbing when she was a teenager. After finishing school, she worked as a nurse but continued to climb in her free time.

After climbing Everest, Gerlinde chose to climb all fourteen of the world's tallest mountains. To make it harder, she climbs without oxygen tanks, which is dangerous because low oxygen can affect how the brain and body work. Gerlinde uses her fame as a climber to help a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.

If we look at the things we have bought in our lives, we can see that not everything is used well: the warm coat we thought was stylish even though we live in a hot country, the old smartphone we stopped using when we got a new one, the car we only drive on weekends, or the guest room that has become a storage room.

Throughout history, many cultures believed that dreams could predict the future. People thought dreams were messages from gods that gave us knowledge. Even now, many people remember a time when they dreamed about something that later happened in real life.

Some of the largest and most costly transportation projects in the world have included building bridges. Bridges are important connections that allow cars, trucks, and trains to cross water, valleys, or other roads. Because of this, they are very important in civil engineering and are closely examined, especially when they fall down.

After being frustrated for weeks, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the problems she had with her team. Her manager just asked if she thought her team was still doing well and what could help her work better with them. Gabriela thought her manager was unclear and didn’t feel he was handling the situation well.

Dogs that live in groups have learned that people are more likely to give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs go to ask for food for everyone. Some dogs have even learned to use the metro to move around their area! Scientists don’t know how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize their favorite places. Another idea is that they understand the names of the stations from the announcements. Either way, people on the metro have gotten used to seeing dogs on the trains, and they mostly don’t notice them.

Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the whole Amazon River. He began at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and reached the end of the river in Brazil after two years and four months, walking 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest has dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, so Ed was always in danger. Fortunately, he only got a lot of mosquito and ant bites.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes each year, which is about four percent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two bigger problems for society and the environment. First, many people are using credit cards to pay for these clothes. British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of what they spend on clothes. Also, people are buying things they don’t need and spending money they don’t have. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing every year, and most of it ends up in landfills.

Ed's walk would not have been possible without technology. He used a radio to ask people in the rainforest for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to help him and guide him through the tough areas. While he walked, Ed wrote a blog about his daily experiences. He used the media attention from his trip to talk about the destruction of the rainforest and to raise money for charities that help the environment and children in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have realized they can make money from the sharing economy and want to use resources that are not being fully used. A popular business model allows companies to create online platforms that connect customers with people who can offer a specific product or service. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their empty rooms and houses for extra income. Another example is Uber, which lets people use their own cars as taxis to earn some extra money in their free time.

One important job of modern zoos is to help breed endangered animals from different countries. In the wild, some rare animals have trouble finding mates and having babies, and they can also be in danger from hunters, losing their homes, and other animals. A good zoo helps these animals live and breed safely. Also, when some wild animals become fewer in number, they can become too similar genetically. Breeding programs help by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild to make the gene pool more diverse.

Both types of accidents are very rare, but boats and trains can make a bridge fall for different reasons. Trains can cause a bridge to fall because they hit it very hard. Boats can cause a bridge to fall because they are very heavy, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to stop bridges from falling is to plan for it. New technologies that find weak spots, safer work areas, and better designs can help reduce these accidents.

At first, Pi is scared of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water and knows he must climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other until only Pi and the tiger are left. Luckily for Pi, the tiger, whom he names Richard Parker, feels sick and does not want to eat him right away.

When Pi is 16, a new government is chosen that his parents do not like. They are worried about the future, so they decide to close the zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family travels by ship to Canada with the animals. During the journey, a big storm happens, and the ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi ends up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a large tiger.

The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults by the American writer Suzanne Collins. It was published in 2008 and has been translated into 26 languages, selling millions of copies worldwide. It is also the first book for young readers to sell over a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie and is very successful, making 152.5 million dollars in its first weekend in North America!

Dreams might be how our mind organizes our thoughts from the day, but they show up in dreams with special meanings. When we are awake, we mostly think in words, like talking to ourselves. But when we sleep, the part of our brain that helps us use language is less active, while the part that deals with emotions is more active.

Having good relationships is very important for happiness. In one study, most happy people had strong connections with friends and family and spent time with them often. You also need at least one person to talk to about your feelings. Just one close friend is enough, along with other friends. It’s not enough to have many friends just to hang out with or talk about things like music or football. That deeper connection is very important. Some people need to learn how to listen better to others to build stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck talked about how our brains can change and how we can get better at skills we might not be good at at first. Many people often praise the final result and natural talents, like saying, "You are good at noticing details" or "You are talented at organizing events." However, research shows that if we focus on how things are done—like praising effort, trying new things, and solving problems—we can help people learn new skills and improve their talents.

The rover checks the air around it from time to time, and in 2014 it found a simple organic molecule called methane, which is also a part of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, so something on Mars must be making more of it. NASA says Mars releases thousands of tons of methane at once, and the amount goes up and down with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

Early in her job, the psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-olds some problems that were a bit too hard. One group liked the challenge and believed they could get better. She called this a 'growth mindset.' But another group felt judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and couldn’t see how to improve. Some of these children said they might cheat later; others looked for someone who did worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films like empty places. This could be an old hospital, a scary house, or a ghost town. There is something about lonely places. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they go away? It is also very quiet, which can be scary. Abandoned places are good for horror films because there is usually no phone signal there.

In horror movies, basements are always scary places. They are often dark and damp, and you can only get to them by a narrow staircase. Something is usually hiding there, or a bad person has hidden their tools. Basements feel creepy, even if nothing is there.

Gary Collins, a policeman who was not working, was watching the London riots on TV. He saw some people he knew and decided to end his holiday early to help identify them. He spent six months looking at CCTV footage and identified 190 people, often just by their eyes. His help was very important for the investigation. Even though there were 200,000 hours of footage, the facial recognition software only found one person.

I find it interesting to think about how we can make our bodies better. Imagine if we could put a computer in our brains! Soon, we might be able to do that and improve our math skills, how we see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more normal.

The talk was interesting, and the speaker made some good points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework when they see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting? She also mentioned how people want to be in many places at once, so they switch between real-life and online chats. I notice this with my daughter and her friends; they meet but often sit quietly, each talking online instead.

There are news stories that make us think the world is more violent, but there is also some good news. From the end of World War II to 1990, there were 30 wars that killed over 100,000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly living together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. Still, the news is not all bad for civilians. Even though violent crime is nine times more likely to cause deaths than political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has spent her life helping human rights and has seen many projects in her country that teach women and girls. However, when these projects end, the women often have nothing left. She realized that Bangladesh needed to be stronger, so she combined her love for climbing and human rights to change how people think about women in her country. She started climbing while working on projects in Tibet and Nepal because most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign is working, and people in her country and around the world are starting to pay attention.

Most people think that developing countries are very poor and have bad leaders, with no chance for change. But this is not true. In fact, many good things are happening. In the last 20 years, over 700 million people have earned more money and left poverty. Also, six million fewer children die from sickness each year, more girls are going to school, and many people now have clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback nicer by putting a positive comment before and after a negative one. But when this happens often, workers might think the positive comments are just hiding the bad ones, making them less valuable. Positive feedback should not just cover up the negative but should help support and encourage good work.

I am part of a group that wants to stop dangerous robots. Forget the scary robots from movies. Right now, machines like drones and robots are already being used to kill people with little help from humans. The next step will be robots that can decide on their own who to kill. I believe this is very wrong and could be dangerous for everyone. We need to be careful about what we let machines do.

More people are learning English than all the other languages together, and English is spoken in the most countries. However, Chinese has the most native speakers. There is not much connection between the number of native speakers and the number of learners, but there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries speak the language.

Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about how you did on the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. When you go into her office on Monday morning, she starts by saying nice things about your work on the project, and you wonder if this is just the usual way to give feedback. You know the feedback sandwich: say something nice, say what you really think, and then say something nice again.

Born in the USA is a fast rock album with catchy songs, but the lyrics are very emotional. The songs tell stories about the struggles of regular people who work hard but don’t get rich or famous. For example, the song Glory Days is about people remembering their youth, while Downbound Train is about a young man who loses his job and his life becomes difficult. You can feel that the artist is sharing real stories from his life. The album shows how talented the artist is.

Lewis wants to increase the number of protected ocean areas from 3 percent to 10 percent to help fix the damage caused by things like overfishing and pollution. He has seen this damage himself during his trips. He has swum over coral reefs that are dying because the water is too warm and has seen empty areas in the Red Sea filled with plastic. Pugh thinks that nature can heal if we give it a chance, but time is running out. If we don’t take care of our oceans, we might face a big problem soon.

Best-selling author Terrie Sharp knows how to tell good stories. She has won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times. She grew up in a place in Glasgow with a lot of crime, where she learned to be quiet and stay safe. She used her skills to write her books, and now she talks on popular daytime shows and at writing events in the UK.

Are things getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker talks about human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker says, is that the values of reason and science are being attacked. When people focus on tribalism, hopelessness, and distrust, we risk harming important things like democracy and global cooperation.

In old horror movies, when the main characters were in trouble, it was hard for them to get help or call the police. Now, with mobile phones, that seems less real. To keep the suspense, there is no phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror movie, you will probably find that you can't call for help when you really need to. Your phone might not have any signal, or the battery might die just when you are trying to call.

In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America were losing their best product, the Gros Michel banana, also called Big Mike. Now, the same thing is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish banana. The Gros Michel banana was popular because it was easy to transport and had a thick skin and sweet taste. United Fruit, the main banana grower and exporter in South America at that time, produced bananas very efficiently by cloning plants instead of growing them from seeds and planting them closely together.

Most spiders have venom that helps them catch their food, not to hurt people. Only 25 types of spiders can harm humans, and while their bites can hurt, they usually are not deadly. The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone since they made an anti-venom in 1981. But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel scared, they can shoot out irritating hairs that can get stuck in your skin or eyes.

This scary movie idea was very popular in horror films from the late 1900s. It begins with a group of teenagers having fun, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At first, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she becomes the strongest and smartest person. The last girl almost always wins.

If we want to understand where our ability to use complex language comes from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. It's not just about brain size; it's also important to know what other things our brains can do and why they changed over time. There are very few physical clues to help us; things left by our ancestors don’t show us what kind of speech they could make. However, we can see that early humans had changes in their mouth, throat, and tongue. By around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

Society tells us that girls should like arts and humanities and leave math and physics for boys. There are not many positive female role models in science for young people to see. Cartoons and stories often show scientists as men. Also, people think that scientists are strange and not good at socializing, or that their work is lonely. These are wrong ideas shown by the media, but they might make girls feel like they don’t belong in science and see it as a boring job. If girls saw more positive female role models in science, it would help them feel more confident and included in those subjects.

The Scallion is a weekly newspaper that is given out for free in faculty buildings, and about 10,000 students read it. It is made by students. A survey shows that university students and staff really like the newspaper for fun, culture, and work experience. Printing the newspapers costs a lot of money. Also, some students find it hard to get a copy because they have to go to the university to pick it up. Another problem is that many copies become litter on campus.

At Girox Foods, about 12 out of every 100 employees leave each year. This number seems high because the usual rate in the industry is 7 out of 100. This report aims to find out why employees feel engaged at work and to suggest ways to make their experience better and keep them working here longer.

The speaker said many true things. I really believe that being more connected can make us feel more alone. My generation, who grew up without technology, knows how to be alone and that it's okay. But for those under 20, it's different. They talk a lot but don’t know what it’s like to be alone and might not learn to enjoy their own company. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be changed, instead of having real conversations with people face to face.
Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If you always mix them, people might not appreciate the good comments. Sometimes, just give positive feedback without adding criticism.

Your dreams can reveal insights about thoughts you weren't aware of. Common dreams, such as flying, falling, losing teeth, or being naked in public, often have similar meanings for most people. However, to truly understand what they mean for you, it's important to connect them to your daily experiences and emotions.

One of the most fascinating examples of wild animals living in a city is the wild dogs of Moscow. Approximately 35,000 wild dogs roam the streets of Moscow. Some of these dogs were born in the wild, while others were once pets that were abandoned. Some dogs live by themselves, while others form packs. In 2010, scientists conducted a study on these dogs and discovered that they have adapted very well to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with humans, and some dogs even seem to understand how traffic lights work.

Wonder is the first novel by RJ Palacio. She explains on her website that the idea for the book came to her after she saw a girl with facial deformities on the street. Wonder has become a bestseller in the United States and has won several awards. Many schools are using it to start discussions about bullying, friendship, and what it means to be different. A film adaptation is in progress, and many people, including myself, are looking forward to seeing what RJ Palacio will write next.

Chloe owns two pet rats called Zena and Roxy. She realizes they are not common pets, and she has lost track of how many times she has patiently explained to others that rats are not dirty and can be wonderful pets if taken care of properly. However, she understands why some people have a negative reaction. She didn’t like rats either until her friend Martin introduced her to his pet rats, and she noticed how loving and intelligent they could be. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she wanted to adopt two of them.

Cape Town can be a risky place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents, while others have been electrocuted by playing with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species, so to protect them and reduce conflicts with humans, the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors. Their job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, but it is difficult to prevent baboons from returning to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.

I work for a global IT company, but since their headquarters is in the United States, I do all my work online from home. This means I don’t waste time commuting or chatting with colleagues. I work on various projects, and this flexibility is very important to me because I can easily take time off for my children’s school performances or to schedule dentist appointments. However, the downside is that without clear office hours, I often end up working late into the evening and sometimes skip dinner to complete my tasks.

In the 1990s, graffiti remained popular, but there was also a significant rise in street art globally. Some artists aimed to make political statements and created works that encouraged people to think about issues like war, inequality, and discrimination. Other street artists were more focused on creating visually appealing art. In South America, many street artists worked in impoverished neighborhoods, bringing color and life to grey city walls.

Social media, magazines, and shop windows constantly show people things to buy, and British consumers are purchasing more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping allows customers to buy things easily without much thought, while major brands sell such inexpensive clothes that they can be treated as disposable items, worn a few times and then discarded.

Sam squinted against the sun as he watched the dust trail from the car heading to the Big House. The horses were kicking and swatting flies, not caring that their owner was visiting for the first time in ten months. Sam waited patiently. Mr. Carter only came out when necessary, which was fine with Sam. The more he stayed out of his boss's way, the longer he would keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped the sweat from his neck, and the damp patches on his shirt formed shapes like those on a map. His skin was already turning red from the June sun, and he had the tan of a man who made money while others did the work.

Many residents in Berlin, Germany, complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel, leading to heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to the protests, the city council decided to take a more peaceful approach to manage the pigs. Instead of shooting them, they constructed fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. It remains to be seen if this strategy will be effective, but it could be a difficult challenge since warmer winters have resulted in a larger pig population than before.

A major inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's interest in Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favorite stories was about Theseus and the Minotaur. In this tale, the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel against this control. As a punishment, King Minos of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete each year. These youths are thrown into a labyrinth and eaten by a monster called the Minotaur. However, one of the boys, Theseus, fights the Minotaur and defeats it. Suzanne views Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic version of Theseus.

By bringing people and animals together, zoos can educate the public about conservation and encourage them to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe place for animals that were mistreated in circuses or abandoned pets. They also conduct important research on animal behavior and how to treat their illnesses.

A new trend is emerging that opposes consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and later spread to the US, where it rejects the excessive spending associated with Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day, people organize protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups facilitate the exchange and repair of items that people already own.

Is graffiti considered art or vandalism? This question depends on your perspective, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is viewed as vandalism. Many street artists have faced police intervention, and some have had to pay fines. City councils often complain about the high costs of removing graffiti from buildings, buses, and trains.

What is the opinion of the art world on graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been an increasing recognition of its value as an art form. Major exhibitions of street art have taken place in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald organized a street art exhibition at a gallery in New York. She defended street artists by stating, "Artists who paint on the street are simply expressing themselves and not causing harm. They deserve appreciation and celebration."

Most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, which adds up to about 2,000 dreams each year. By the time someone reaches 80 years old, they might have experienced around 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 percent of them, we still remember a few thousand dreams throughout our lives. It’s not hard to believe that a dream could be followed by a similar event in real life, especially if the dream is about something common in our daily lives.

The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America has been destroyed. The country is called Panem and consists of twelve poor districts that are ruled by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol has complete control over the nation. Each district produces different resources for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, supplies all the coal for the country. There was once a thirteenth district, but it rebelled against the Capitol in the past and was destroyed.

Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun to invade residential areas near the city to find food. They open garbage bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some daring baboons have even entered homes and taken food from kitchens! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked many pets, so it is understandable that many city residents do not welcome them.

A lot of accidents happen during bridge construction. These accidents are usually caused by mistakes from the engineers, such as miscalculations. The bridge can collapse under its own weight, which can be fatal for the workers who are on it at that moment.

George Lucas was one of the early film directors to base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically, the hero begins with an ordinary life, but an event occurs that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the start of Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it serves as the call to adventure that begins his journey.

Another proposed way to defend against an asteroid heading towards Earth is to use a nuclear weapon to blow it up. While it may seem like a storyline from a movie, as seen in the 1998 film Armageddon, the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real proposal from NASA. The plan involves firing eight-ton rockets at an approaching asteroid to try to change its course. If the asteroid is too close for this method to be effective, the rockets would instead carry nuclear bombs to destroy it.

According to Campbell, the hero initially refuses the call to adventure, but a mentor appears to help them, leading them to decide to enter the 'special world' where the adventure occurs. The next stage involves facing tests, battling enemies, and meeting friends as the hero prepares for their greatest challenge. For Luke, Obi-Wan is the mentor, Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO are his friends, and Darth Vader is the enemy in the special world of the Death Star.

Items that are not used often may seem worthless to some, but they can be valuable to others. With the rise of the internet, online communities have discovered ways to profit from sharing these underused items. Thanks to websites and social media groups that help buy and sell second-hand goods, peer-to-peer sharing has become easier than ever. This concept is known as the sharing economy.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main theories about dreams became popular. One theory suggested that dreams represent things we are not aware of in our conscious mind. Freud believed that by understanding our dreams, we could uncover our hidden feelings and the issues they create. The other theory was quite different; it claimed that dreams are simply random brain activity while we organize memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we attempt to make sense of these random images and feelings and create a story from them.

I am a freelancer, which means I work for myself. This is great because I can control my work and how I spend my time. At first, I worked from home, but I found it difficult to concentrate because there were too many distractions, like housework, wanting another cup of tea, and family members needing my attention. I then tried working at a nearby café, but the Wi-Fi connection was not good, and I ended up drinking too much coffee. In the end, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers. I enjoyed getting dressed for work in the morning and being able to focus in an office setting.

NASA's ability to find the remaining middle-sized near-Earth objects (NEOs) depends on securing funding to build NEOCam, a 0.5-meter space telescope that uses infrared light to detect asteroids. If they receive the funding, they could likely achieve this goal in ten years. After identifying these asteroids, the planetary defense team would still need to determine how to protect the planet from the most concerning asteroids, known as potentially hazardous asteroids (PHAs).

The 'buy nothing' trend has become popular among social media influencers who typically share recommendations for clothing and make-up. Some YouTube stars now encourage their viewers to avoid buying anything for as long as a year. Two friends in Canada dedicated a year to only purchasing food. During the first three months, they learned to live without buying electronics, clothes, or household items. In the next phase, they stopped using services like haircuts, dining out, or buying gas for their cars. By the end of the year, they had saved $55,000.

Pi values religion a lot. Although his family practices Hinduism, he is curious about other faiths and befriends a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi claims he wants to be Hindu, Muslim, and Christian all at once. When his family and teachers urge him to choose just one religion, Pi responds, "I just want to love God." From that point on, his family and teachers allow him to make his own decisions regarding religion.

Some people think that writing down your dreams can help you experience lucid dreaming. Lucid dreams are when you realize you are dreaming and can make choices that change what happens in the dream. This means you could turn a nightmare into a pleasant dream or guide the story of your dream like a film director. So, instead of just figuring out what your dreams mean, you will be creating them, although you might still want to have some dreams that let your subconscious express what you are thinking!

Many people may not realize they contribute to the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. However, charity shops cannot sell all of those clothes. 'Fast fashion' quickly goes out of style and is often too poor in quality to be recycled; people are not interested in buying it second-hand. As a result, large amounts end up in landfills, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are exported, leading to further economic and environmental challenges.

Some adventurers are not satisfied with just one incredible trip. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountain on each continent, cycled across Canada, and completed a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in extreme heat. However, her most impressive journey was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. Many would have given up after that, but Meagan decided to continue. She reached the South Pole forty days later, pulling a sled with her tent and food through freezing temperatures and ice storms.

Blek le Rat started by painting rats on the walls of his hometown, Paris. Today, he aims to raise awareness about various social issues. He creates artworks of homeless individuals in large cities to encourage people to consider the problem of homelessness.

In certain areas, local councils have attempted to encourage artists to avoid painting graffiti on random walls by providing designated spaces for their work. Taiwan has 'graffiti zones' where artists can freely express themselves. In São Paulo, Brazil, the city council has allowed some graffiti artists to paint on subway trains.

Faith47 is an artist from Cape Town, South Africa. She creates large, colorful paintings of people and animals and enjoys discovering various locations. Her artwork can be seen on sidewalks, in abandoned factories, and on old cars. She appreciates that most street art is temporary and will eventually be removed by the weather or city cleaners. For her, this represents how life is full of changes, with cycles of endings and new beginnings.

In her previous workplace, Gabriela was accustomed to a culture with a high power distance, where power and authority are respected, and everyone has a specific role. In this culture, leaders make important decisions and are rarely questioned. However, her Swedish team is familiar with a low power distance culture, where employees often work together with their managers to find solutions and make decisions. In this environment, leaders act as coaches or mentors, encouraging independent thinking and welcoming challenges.

When Gabriela realized there were cultural differences between her and her team, she took the step to have an open conversation with them about their feelings regarding her leadership. Her team was glad to share their opinions and mentioned that they were not accustomed to being told what to do. They preferred having more freedom to take initiative and be creative. When Gabriela specified exactly what she needed them to do, they felt that she didn't trust their abilities. They recognized that Gabriela took their attempts to challenge or change her decisions personally, and they were able to explain that this was how they had always worked.

Os Gêmeos são irmãos gêmeos idênticos que vêm de São Paulo. Eles fazem pinturas que vão desde pequenas tags até enormes e coloridas imagens de pessoas nas laterais de prédios. Seu trabalho é muitas vezes tão grande que precisam de guindastes para conseguir pintar. Em 2007, eles cobriram todo um castelo na Escócia com suas pinturas.

Throughout history, people have painted and written on walls. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe created paintings of animals and humans in caves. Graffiti has been discovered on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In Pompeii, a Roman town, archaeologists found many examples of graffiti written in Latin, which include religious, political, and romantic messages, as well as some magic spells!

Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If so, you are not alone. Every year, thousands of people attempt to climb the highest mountains or walk across entire continents. Unlike the explorers of the past who relied on maps and compasses, today’s adventurers use modern technology such as GPS and satellite phones. Many of these adventurers are passionate about nature and use their journeys to raise awareness about various environmental issues, while others are eager to help those in need and raise funds for charities.

The first project is called DART, which means the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. There are plans to test DART on the moon of an asteroid named Didymos. This moon, known as 'Didymoon,' is 150 meters wide and orbits its larger asteroid, which is 800 meters wide. They hope that the impact of DART will change Didymoon's orbit enough for telescopes on Earth to detect it.

The main character of the story is a sixteen-year-old girl named Katniss Everdeen. After losing her father in a mining accident, she has to provide food for her family. She hunts in the woods around District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very skilled with a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is selected as one of the tributes, Katniss volunteers to take her place. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta, and Katniss finds herself in a complicated relationship with him.

Writing about your dreams will help you remember more details. Consider the people and places in your dreams, as they may add to their meaning. After a week, you might be surprised by how much you have written down. You can then start to connect your dreams to the events and feelings in your everyday life.

Historically, many bridges were constructed from wood, making them more likely to catch fire. This was especially common with old train bridges, where sparks from the steel wheels and tracks could sometimes ignite a fire and destroy the bridge.

It is difficult to predict how street art will evolve in the future, but we can see some trends emerging. Most street artists are young individuals who create art in their local areas, but an increasing number are traveling and working internationally. Additionally, many artists are using the internet to connect and share images of their work. The art community is also beginning to acknowledge street art as a valid form of art. While the future of street art is uncertain, it is clear that it is here to stay!

Suzanne has always found war news upsetting. As a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Although her mother tried to protect her by not discussing the war, she still watched news programs about it and knew her dad was involved. This was a very frightening experience for her.

In a global survey by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), more than 40,000 millennials and non-millennials provided their opinions on workplace culture, communication styles, pay structures, career development, and work-life balance. Additionally, a separate global survey by Deloitte involved over 10,000 millennials discussing their views on the challenges and opportunities in the modern workplace.

Erik Weihenmayer, an adventurer from the United States, has ridden a bike through the deserts of Morocco, kayaked in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. Remarkably, he has been blind since he was 13. In addition to his adventures, he encourages people with disabilities to lead active lives and organizes climbing trips for young blind people.

Online platforms are allowing people to make some extra money easily. For instance, busy parents might not have sold their children's old items at local markets before, but now they can sell barely used baby clothes and expensive baby gear online to get some money back.

Pi and Richard Parker spend 227 days in a lifeboat. They experience hunger, illness, and exhaustion. They face violent storms and the intense heat of the Pacific sun, but they manage to survive. At times, Pi finds comfort in his three religions, but he also feels deep loneliness and despair. Eventually, he sees the Mexican coast on the horizon, and everything changes. I won’t spoil the ending, so you will need to read the book to discover what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they finally see land.

Chloe got home from school, made herself a cup of coffee, and took it to her bedroom. Although she had some homework to do, she decided to wait and enjoy the quiet hour before her parents came home. She liked this time because the house would soon be filled with sounds of conversation, the TV, or her dad listening to jazz while he cooked dinner. She also enjoyed playing with her pet rats during this peaceful time.

In 2010, NASA's planetary defense team identified and recorded 90 percent of the asteroids near Earth that are 1 kilometer wide. These 'near-Earth objects' are the size of mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometers of Earth's orbit. NASA estimates that there are about 50 more to log, and states that none of the 887 known asteroids pose a significant threat to our planet.

Auggie chooses to go to school, but his first day is really tough. Like any child starting at a new school, he feels anxious. However, because of his appearance, it becomes a painful experience. No one wants to sit next to him, and he notices other kids staring or whispering about him. Fortunately, he makes friends with Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he talks to at lunch. But it’s not just the first day that is difficult. Auggie soon discovers that his classmates don’t want to touch him because they are afraid of catching 'the plague'. As the school year goes on, Auggie experiences many highs and lows until an unexpected and traumatic event at a school camp changes everything completely.

The two men gazed toward the northern side of the property, which seemed to stretch endlessly. The fences were almost invisible from their position. A bored teenage boy wouldn’t be able to escape on foot. Sam observed the largest horse, kicking the ground with its heavy hooves, and wondered if the boy could ride. A skilled rider could easily find trouble out there, far from anyone else. However, someone who knew nothing about horses might face even greater trouble if they tried to get away from their father.

Over 4,000 climbers, aged from thirteen to eighty, have successfully reached the summit of Everest. Although climbing high mountains in freezing temperatures and severe storms remains very dangerous, the world's top climbers are now seeking new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria developed a passion for mountain climbing as a teenager. After she graduated from school, she worked as a nurse while still pursuing climbing in her spare time.

After successfully climbing Everest, Gerlinde decided to climb all fourteen of the world's 8,000-meter peaks. To make the challenge greater, she climbs without using oxygen tanks, which is risky because low oxygen levels at high altitudes can affect brain and body functions. Gerlinde also uses her fame as a climber to support a charity that helps poor children and orphans in Nepal.

When we think about the things we have bought over the years, we can see that not everything is being used properly: the thick coat we thought was fashionable even though we live in a tropical country, the smartphone we stopped using after getting the latest model, the car that we only use on weekends, or the guest room that has turned into a storeroom.

Throughout history and in different cultures, dreams have been linked to prophecy. People believed that dreams were messages from the gods that provided knowledge or insight. Even today, many people can remember a time when they dreamed about an event, place, or person, and then that dream came true later.

Some of the largest and most expensive transportation projects globally have involved the construction of bridges. Bridges serve as essential connections that enable cars, trucks, and trains to cross over water, mountain gorges, or other roads. Therefore, they are a vital part of civil engineering and are carefully monitored, particularly when they collapse.

After weeks of frustration, Gabriela sent an email to her Swedish manager about the problems she was having with her team. Her manager simply asked if she believed her team was still performing well and what could help her collaborate better with her team members. Gabriela found her manager to be vague and felt that he was not managing the situation effectively.

Dogs that live in packs have learned that humans tend to give food to smaller, cuter dogs, so those dogs are sent to beg for food for the entire pack. Some dogs have even figured out how to use the metro system to travel around their territory! Scientists are unsure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One theory is that they use their strong sense of smell to recognize the scents of their favorite places. Another possibility is that they have learned to recognize the names of stations from the announcements. Regardless, metro passengers have become so accustomed to seeing dogs on the trains that they often go unnoticed by locals.

Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the entire length of the Amazon River. He started at a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and arrived at the river's mouth in Brazil after two years and four months, having walked 6,000 kilometers. The Amazon rainforest is home to dangerous animals like poisonous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars, which meant Ed faced constant danger. Luckily, he survived with just a few thousand bites from mosquitoes and ants.

In Britain, the average person spends over £1,000 on new clothes every year, which is around four percent of their income. While this might not seem like a lot, it reveals two more serious issues for society and the environment. First, a large part of this spending is done using credit cards. Currently, British adults owe about £670 each to credit card companies, which is 66 percent of their average clothing budget. Additionally, people are not only spending money they don’t have, but they are also buying things they don’t really need. Britain discards 300,000 tons of clothing each year, most of which goes to landfills.

Ed's walk would have been impossible without technology. He used a radio to communicate with the people in the rainforest, asking for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped guide him through the hardest parts of the journey. As he walked, Ed wrote a blog to document his daily experiences. He took advantage of the media's interest in his trip to raise awareness about the destruction of the rainforest and to gather funds for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.

Businesses have recognized the profit potential of the sharing economy and are looking to benefit from underused resources. A popular business model involves companies providing online platforms that connect customers with those who can offer specific products or services. For instance, Airbnb acts as a middleman, allowing people to rent out their unused rooms and houses for extra income. Similarly, Uber encourages individuals to use their personal cars as taxis to earn additional money during their free time.

One of the key roles of modern zoos is to support breeding programs for endangered species. In the wild, many rare animals struggle to find mates and reproduce, and they are also at risk from poachers, habitat loss, and predators. A good zoo provides a safe environment for these animals to live and breed. Additionally, as the numbers of some wild species decline, there is a greater risk of them becoming too genetically similar. Breeding programs act as a safeguard by allowing zoo-bred animals to be released into the wild, which helps increase genetic diversity.

Both types of accidents are quite rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to collapse for different reasons. With trains, it is the speed of the impact that can lead to a bridge falling. With boats, their large weight can cause a collapse, even if they are moving slowly. The best way to prevent bridge failures is to plan for them. Modern technologies that can detect structural weaknesses, safer working conditions, and improved designs can all help reduce these serious accidents.

At first, Pi is afraid of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers that there are hungry sharks in the water and realizes he has to climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other until only Pi and the tiger remain. Fortunately for Pi, the tiger, whom he names Richard Parker, is seasick and is not interested in eating him at that moment.

When Pi turns 16, a new government is elected that his parents do not support. Concerned about what will happen next, Pi's parents decide to shut down the zoo and emigrate to Canada. They sell some of the animals to zoos in North America and travel by ship to Canada with the remaining animals. Unfortunately, a terrible storm occurs, and the ship sinks. Tragically, Pi's family and the sailors drown, but Pi finds himself in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and a huge tiger.

The Hunger Games is a highly successful book for teenagers and young adults written by American author Suzanne Collins. Since its release in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies globally. It was also the first book aimed at young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games has been adapted into a major Hollywood film, which has also been very successful, earning 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America alone!

Dreams might be the result of our mind organizing the thoughts we have during the day, but they often appear in dreams with symbolic meanings. When we are awake, our thoughts usually come to us as words, like conversations we have with ourselves. However, when we sleep, the part of our brain that controls language becomes less active, while the part that manages emotions becomes more active.

Good relationships are a key part of being happy. In a study, most happy people were found to have strong connections with friends and family, and they made sure to spend time with them regularly. It's also important to have at least one person to talk to about personal feelings, which is called 'self-disclosure.' Just one close friend is enough, along with a network of other relationships. Having many friends to do activities with or chat about music or football is not enough; that deeper connection is essential. Some people need to improve their listening skills to develop stronger relationships.

Psychologist Carol Dweck discussed how the brain can change and how we can improve skills we may not have been good at initially. Many people tend to give praise based on the final results and natural abilities, such as saying, "You have a great eye for detail" or "You are talented at organizing events." However, research indicates that by focusing on the process—praising effort, experimentation, and problem-solving—we can promote the development of new skills and the ongoing improvement of existing talents.

The rover periodically analyzes the air around it, and in 2014, it discovered methane, a basic organic molecule and a key component of natural gas. Methane only lasts for a few hundred years, which suggests that something on Mars is producing more of it. According to NASA, Mars emits thousands of tons of methane at once, and the levels fluctuate with the seasons, almost as if the planet is breathing.

Early in her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were a little too difficult for them. One group responded positively, saying they enjoyed challenges and believed they could improve their abilities. She described this as having a 'growth mindset.' However, another group felt that their intelligence was being judged and thought they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and struggled to see how they could get better. Some of these children mentioned they might cheat in the future, while others looked for someone who performed worse than them to feel better about themselves.

Horror films often take place in uninhabited locations, such as abandoned hospitals, creepy empty houses, or ghost towns. There is something intriguing about these lonely places. What was life like when people lived there? Why did they leave? The silence can also be quite frightening. Additionally, abandoned places are useful for horror film directors because it makes sense that there would be no phone coverage there.

In horror films, basements are always portrayed as scary places. They are often where something is hiding or where the villain keeps their tools. Basements tend to be dark and damp, and you can only access them through a narrow staircase. They feel creepy, even when there is nothing down there.

Gary Collins, an off-duty police officer, was watching the London riots on TV when he recognized several individuals. He cut his holiday short to assist with their identification. Over six months, he reviewed CCTV footage and successfully identified 190 people, often just by looking at their eyes. His contribution was crucial to the investigation, especially since the facial recognition software could only identify one person out of 200,000 hours of footage.

I think it's really interesting to think about how we can speed up our evolution by improving our bodies. Imagine if we could implant a computer in our brains! Soon, we might be able to do that and enhance our math skills, our ability to see and hear, and our memory. This idea will become more usual in the future.

The talk was really interesting, and the speaker made some important points. For example, how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing their homework when they see their parents posting on social media while cooking or waiting at a red light? She also pointed out that people often want to be in multiple places at once, so they switch between real-life conversations and online chats. I see this happening with my teenage daughter and her friends; they meet up but often sit in silence while each is engaged in a different online conversation.

While some news stories suggest that the world is becoming more violent, there is also some positive news. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that resulted in over 100,000 deaths. Nowadays, although there are still civil wars, countries are generally co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has increased in recent years, and since World War II, more civilians have died in wars than soldiers. On a brighter note, even though deaths from violent crime are nine times more likely than those from political conflict, the global murder rate has slightly decreased, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

Wasfia has devoted her life to supporting human rights and has observed many international projects in her country aimed at educating and training women and girls. Unfortunately, when these projects end, the women are often left with nothing. Realizing that Bangladesh needed to assert itself, she combined her passions for mountaineering and human rights to change attitudes towards women in her country. She began climbing while working on humanitarian campaigns in Tibet and Nepal, as most people in flat Bangladesh have never seen a mountain. Her campaign appears to be effective, as people in her country and around the world are starting to take notice.

Many people believe that developing countries are in a bad situation, facing extreme poverty, ruled by dictators, and lacking hope for real change. However, this is not accurate. In reality, a significant transformation is taking place. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have improved their income and escaped poverty. Furthermore, six million fewer children die from diseases each year, millions more girls are attending school, and many people have gained access to clean water.

Many managers try to make their feedback more positive by placing a negative comment between two positive ones. However, if this becomes a habit, employees may start to see positive feedback as just a way to cover up the negatives, which reduces its importance. Instead, positive feedback should be used to truly support and motivate good performance.

I am a member of a campaign to stop dangerous robots.
